subject: Data disposition and tenant TTL — security questionnaire response (hosted API)
messages:
From: Amanda Li <amanda.li@skybridge.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Cc: security@skybridge.com
Date: 2028-08-25T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Security questionnaire — tenant TTL/retain & legal hold follow-ups

Jonas,

Thanks for the initial questionnaire. A couple of follow-ups from our risk team so we can close the compliance review: 

1) We need a precise definition of "tenant TTL" for hosted API customers. Does TTL remove all customer data (request payloads, evaluations, cached prefixes, logs) or only model inputs/outputs?

2) In the event of a legal hold, can you confirm whether retention overrides TTL, and whether Redwood preserves a forensically verifiable snapshot (including backups) or only prevents scheduled deletion?

3) Backup retention — how long are backups retained, where are they stored, and are they subject to the same geofencing controls as primary data?

We've got an internal deadline to sign off next Friday. Appreciate any detail you can provide and any artifacts (attestation, playbook) we can attach to our security binder.

Thanks,
Amanda Li
Security & Compliance Manager
Skybridge Health

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Amanda Li <amanda.li@skybridge.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-08-26T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Security questionnaire — tenant TTL/retain & legal hold follow-ups

Amanda — thanks for the clear list. I've summarized answers below and attached a short tenant TTL summary PDF and a deletion attestation template you can include in your binder. High level first, details after.

TL;DR:
- Tenant TTL: when a tenant requests deletion or TTL expiration, Redwood removes all customer identifiable data stored in the hosted API plane — that includes request payloads, generated outputs, prefix/KV caches associated with the tenant, and metadata used for billing/usage aggregation.
- Backups: backups are retained for a limited, configurable window (default 30 days) and are encrypted and region-bound to the same geofence as the tenant. Backups are covered by the same data residency controls.
- Legal hold: legal hold overrides scheduled TTL deletion. When a legal hold is applied, Redwood prevents automatic deletion and creates an auditable hold record. We do NOT create new permanent copies beyond existing backups unless specifically requested under an eDiscovery export request.

See inline details and operational notes below. If you want, Karthik can step through the playbook with your ops team this week.

Best,
Jonas
Director, Security & Trust
Redwood Inference

---

Details: 
1) What "tenant TTL" removes
- Primary data: All customer-submitted payloads (text, attachments referenced in requests) and model outputs stored in our hosted API long-term stores are removed at TTL expiration or on tenant deletion request.
- Operational caches: Inference prefix/KV caches associated with tenant sessions are evicted immediately during delete flows; ephemeral caches (per-request) already expire within minutes and are cleaned automatically.
- Logs & telemetry: We keep operational logs used for platform health and billing in a minimized form. Full request/response payload logs used for debugging are scrubbed as part of the deletion flow. Aggregated metrics (e.g., token counts by model) are retained in anonymized form for 180 days for product telemetry.

2) Backups
- Frequency & retention: Backups are incremental snapshots of multi-tenant stores taken daily. Default retention is 30 days; configurable up to 90 days under contractual addendum.
- Storage & residency: Encrypted at rest with customer-key option (KMS) and stored in the same cloud region/geofence as the tenant; backups inherit geofencing and region lock controls.
- Restoration & deletion: When a tenant delete is initiated, we enumerate backups containing the tenant's records and either expunge the tenant's segments (preferred) or, if segment-level removal is infeasible due to snapshot format, we expire the snapshot and ensure it falls out of retention window (engineered to meet contractual timelines). We provide attestations for removal steps.

3) Legal hold and eDiscovery
- Applying a legal hold: When Skybridge requests a legal hold, Redwood creates an immutable hold record with a timestamp, scope, and requesting contact. Automatic TTL pipelines are paused for elements covered by the hold.
- What we preserve: We preserve the data in-place and mark it as "on hold"; we do not spin up additional long-term copies unless you ask for an archive export.
- Forensic exports: If you require a forensically packaged export (hashes, chain-of-custody), we can produce an export-engagement (project) with an agreed scope and delivery SLA. That work is treated as a professional services engagement and will include an export artifact and attestation.

4) Auditability & attestations
- Deletion logs: All deletion operations produce an immutable audit event (who requested, operator id, timestamp, affected tenant id, steps executed).
- Attestation: See attached deletion-attestation-template.docx. For customers with stricter compliance needs we provide signed attestation statements upon request.

5) Edge cases
- Long-tail caches: Third-party caches (CDNs, partner integrations) are outside Redwood's hosted API control; we provide guidance and controls to limit propagation and include recommendations in the playbook.
- Snapshots in immutable object stores: Where snapshot formats prevent in-place edits, we rely on retention expiration plus per-tenant access revocation and attest to the expiration schedule.

Attachments: redwood-tenant-ttl-summary.pdf (high-level flow), deletion-attestation-template.docx (attestation language you can include).

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Amanda Li <amanda.li@skybridge.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-08-28T08:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Security questionnaire — tenant TTL/retain & legal hold follow-ups

Amanda — quick technical clarifications to the questions above that your engineers requested: 

- Cache eviction timing: Prefix/KV caches bound to a tenant are evicted within 60 seconds of the deletion workflow starting. We log the eviction event to the tenant audit trail.
- Backup expunge approach: For service-level snapshots where we cannot surgically remove a tenant segment, the flow is: 1) identify snapshots containing tenant records; 2) schedule snapshot for early expiration and mark as inaccessible to tenant identifiers; 3) create audit entry mapping snapshot IDs to the deletion action. This gives you both a defensible removal timeline and immutable evidence.
- Data in analytics/ML retrain sets: We do not include customer-identifiable data from hosted API requests in model training sets by default. Any telemetry used is aggregated and anonymized; inclusion in training datasets requires an explicit opt-in.

If helpful, I can host a 30-min technical walkthrough with one of your platform engineers Wednesday or Thursday.

Thanks,
Karthik
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>

Amanda — adding operational timelines you can reference in your security binder: 

- Standard deletion SLA: 30 calendar days from confirmed request to complete tenant data removal across primary stores; this includes enumeration and backup expiry steps.
- Expedited deletion: Available as an add-on (10 business days) with an expedited snapshot purge process — we'll include scope and pricing in the addendum if you want to proceed.
- Legal hold processing: Acknowledgement within 2 business days; hold applied within 24 hours of acknowledgement. For forensic export projects we will provide a project plan within 3 business days of request.

I'll coordinate contracting language if Skybridge wants expedited retention windows or a backup-retention cap.

Cheers,
Ben Carter
Enterprise Account Executive
Redwood Inference
